evidence_map.basis_quote: The administration’s workforce reductions escalated in February 2025, when the Office of Personnel Management instructed agencies to review probationary employees and the White House pressed for broad cuts. Probationary workers are generally new hires or employees in a new position who have not completed a trial period; they can have fewer appeal rights than career civil servants, but agencies still must follow applicable laws and procedures. Thousands of employees received termination notices, including workers at the Forest Service and other departments. Reporting described confusion over notices, reversals and whether agencies had completed the dismissals. The administration said it was removing employees it considered noncritical and reducing federal spending. Unions and nonprofit groups challenged the mass-firing approach, arguing that the government had bypassed required procedures. A federal judge temporarily blocked some directives in February, while the litigation did not amount to a blanket finding about every individual termination. The reported effort began after Trump’s inauguration, so it should not be attributed to his transition team or described as advance implementation of Schedule F without evidence.
